title: San Francisco Scores $41 Million for Major Muni Metro Train Control Upgrade That Runs on Floppy Disk - NewsBreak
text: San Francisco’s Muni Metro is on track for a major modernization, thanks to a $41 million grant awarded by the California Transportation Commission. The funds come from the state’s Solutions for Congested Corridors Program and will help the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency improve the Muni Metro system with a modern train control upgrade. The project will overhaul the current outdated train control system and install a new, wireless Communications-Based Train Control system citywide. The SFMTA emphasized that this upgrade is critical for keeping trains running safely and efficiently across San Francisco. According to the SFMTA, Muni Metro is now the fourth busiest light rail system in the United States and serves as a major transit hub for the Bay Area, connecting with systems such as BART, Caltrain, SamTrans, and Golden Gate Transit. “A safe and strong transportation system is critical to our city's recovery,” said San Francisco Mayor Lurie in a statement provided by the city. “As we are working hard to keep Muni running safely and efficiently, this funding will help us deliver the services San Franciscans rely on. Thank you to our state partners for supporting San Francisco's comeback with this investment in Muni.” Julie Kirshbaum, the SFMTA’s Director of Transportation, described the funding as a big win. “This is the first time the SFMTA has pursued a SCCP grant and it’s a major achievement to have won,” said Kirshbaum. “These funds are vital to completing critical work that cannot be deferred and will help the SFMTA deliver a project that improves daily rail service for riders from across the Bay Area by improving Muni Metro reliability citywide.” Dan Howard, Project Manager for the Train Control Upgrade Project, highlighted the regional impact. “Muni serves as a hub for Bay Area-wide transit,” said Howard. “Modern train control will facilitate smoother connections to BART, AC Transit, SamTrans, Caltrain, Golden Gate Transit ferries and the future California High-Speed Rail terminus at the Salesforce Transit Center.” The upgrade will begin in San Francisco’s Mission Bay and Embarcadero neighborhoods with on-street rail improvements. Subway upgrades will follow in 2026, with full system modernization expected by 2032, according to the SFMTA.
